Shawn Timothy Nelson (August 21, 1959 – May 17, 1995) was a U.S. Army veteran, unemployed plumber and meth addict who stole a 57 ton M60A3 Patton tank from a United States National Guard Armory in San Diego, California, and went on a rampage on May 17, 1995.

Nelson drove through an open gate at the Armory and used a crowbar to break open the tank hatch. The tank started with a push button and did not require an ignition key. As he lowered himself into the tank, he was finally noticed by a guardsman, who approached but with little chance of stopping him, he rushed to call police. As ammunition was kept in another building, none of the vehicle's weapons could be loaded or used.

Nelson led police on a 23-minute, televised chase through the streets San Diego. The tank had a top speed of 30 miles per hour (48 km/h). The tank easily plowed through road signs, traffic lights, fire hydrants and crushed several parked vehicles. He even attempted to knock down a bridge by running into the supports, but gave up after he failed to topple it with the first few hits. He eventually became caught on a concrete median of State Route 163, as he attempted to cross the median into the oncoming traffic. Four police officers climbed onto the tank and were able to open the hatch. The officers ordered Nelson to surrender, but he said nothing and began lurching the tank back and forth in attempt to free it from the median. One of the officers then leaned in and shot Nelson, who later died in hospital.
